channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Employment – Fee reduction – Title VII
item.description: Where a plaintiff who won a jury verdict on a retaliation claim under Title VII has challenged the trial judge’s decision to reduce her counsel fees, it was not an abuse of discretion for the judge to exclude “generic” time entries from the lodestar calculation and to reduce the award by 20 percent based on the plaintiff's limited success.

item.title: Immigration – Persecution
item.description: Where the Board of Immigration Appeals affirmed the denial of a petitioner’s applications for asylum, withholding of removal, and protection under the Convention Against Torture, her petition for review should be denied because the petitioner did not carry her burden of establishing that she (1) experienced past persecution or (2) has a well-founded fear of future persecution upon removal to Brazil.

item.title: Bankruptcy – Loss of assets – Discharge denial
item.description: Where a U.S. Bankruptcy Court judge found that appellant debtors did not satisfactorily explain the disposition of their assets and consequentially denied them a discharge, that decision should be affirmed despite the debtors’ argument that 11 U.S.C. §727(a)(5) only permits denial of a discharge when the lost assets at issue are substantial.

item.title: AI-induced privilege waiver rattles lawyers everywhere
item.description: A federal judge in U.S. v. Heppner ruled a client’s AI communications with Claude are not protected by attorney-client privilege or work product doctrine.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy’s defense seeks two-phase murder trial
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's defense requests a bifurcated trial for the murder of her three children, separating guilt and mental health phases.

item.title: Criminal – Bad acts instruction
item.description: Where a defendant was convicted of one count of indecent assault and battery on a person over age 14, the conviction must be vacated because it was prejudicial error not to provide a jury instruction on bad acts after the defendant requested such an instruction.

item.title: Parent and child – Termination – Reasonable efforts
item.description: Where a mother’s parental rights were terminated by a Juvenile Court judge, the termination decree should be affirmed because the mother has waived her argument that the judge erred in ruling that the Department of Children and Families made reasonable efforts to prevent or eliminate the need for removal from the home.

item.title: Municipal – Opioids – Public nuisance
item.description: Where the city of Boston brought suit alleging that two pharmacy benefit managers violated Massachusetts public nuisance law by colluding with opioid manufacturers to misrepresent the risks of such drugs, the dismissal of the public nuisance claim as time-barred should be affirmed because the lower court committed no error in holding that the claim was not tolled under G.L.c. 260, §12

item.title: Education – Corporal punishment
item.description: Where a substantive due process claim has been brought against a defendant teacher, his motion to dismiss on qualified immunity grounds should be denied because the complaint adequately pleads a conscience-shocking violation of the plaintiff student’s right to be free from excessive corporal punishment, a right that was clearly established at the time of the teacher’s alleged misconduct.

item.title: Immigration – Employment authorization
item.description: Where two plaintiffs, one of whom is a Venezuelan national living and working in Massachusetts on a valid H-1B visa, have filed an emergency motion for preliminary injunction requiring adjudication of a pending application for employment authorization, their motion should be allowed because they are likely to succeed on their claim that the Department of Homeland Security’s two policy memoranda (PM-602-0192 and PM-602-0194) imposing a hold on adjudicating applications are arbitrary and capriciou
